editorNote: GitHub's postmortem on its nearly 8-hour outage lands the same week a compromised Rust crate turned routine builds into malware delivery — two reminders that the infrastructure underneath the AI boom is still held together by very human capacity planning and account security. Meanwhile Ramp's enterprise spending data shows OpenAI clawing back share from Anthropic, and a new audit finds that several flavors of language-model self-training don't actually make the model smarter once you control for it properly.

stories.headline: GitHub's August 17 outage lasted nearly 8 hours after a capacity failure in its Central US data center
stories.summary: GitHub says a critical infrastructure component in its Central US data center 'failed to scale' against a new traffic peak, breaking authentication and cascading into Actions, APIs, pull requests, issues and Copilot for 7 hours and 47 minutes; a client-side retry loop in Copilot further complicated recovery. Monthly commits had doubled from 1.4 billion in April to 2.9 billion, and GitHub says it has since added over 3 million CPU cores and 120 petabytes of storage and is isolating critical systems to stop cascading failures.
stories.whyItMatters: It was GitHub's second major incident this month, and the company is now committing to capacity and retry-storm fixes rather than treating the outage as one-off bad luck.

sourceLinks.title: The August 17 outage and the work ahead - GitHub Blog

stories.headline: A compromised maintainer account pushed build-time malware through the arrayref Rust crate
stories.summary: A hijacked account published a malicious arrayref 0.3.10 to crates.io that pulled in a typosquatted 'proc-macro1' dependency; its build script downloaded and ran platform-specific payloads — a detached binary on Unix, a PowerShell/VBScript launcher on Windows — that phoned home to a hardcoded C2 address, executing the moment a project was compiled rather than run. arrayref has roughly 245 million all-time downloads and sits deep in dependency trees including GUI frameworks like egui and iced; crates.io has since pulled the malicious versions and a RustSec advisory documents the indicators of compromise.
stories.whyItMatters: Because the payload runs at compile time, simply building an affected project — not even running it — was enough to trigger the malware.

sourceLinks.title: Malicious Rust crate arrayref/proc-macro1 build-time malware - SafeDep

stories.headline: OpenAI claws back enterprise share from Anthropic, Ramp data shows
stories.summary: Data from corporate card issuer Ramp, tracking over 70,000 U.S. businesses, shows Anthropic's share of paying AI customers grew from 41% to about 44% between May and July while OpenAI grew from 39% to about 40% — but OpenAI is now growing faster, which Ramp economist Ara Kharazian attributes to strong reception for GPT-5.6 Sol among developers. Over 56% of Ramp's business customers now pay for AI services as of July.
stories.whyItMatters: Ramp's data shows enterprise AI spending is expanding overall, but which vendor gets it is volatile and tracks closely with each lab's latest model release.

sourceLinks.title: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates - TechCrunch

stories.headline: "Phantom Gains" audit finds most self-training methods don't actually make models smarter
stories.summary: Researchers ran three rounds of self-training on Qwen3-8B against a frozen control processed identically, and found seven distinct measurement failures that can flip a reported gain into a false positive when no control is used. Once measured against a proper null distribution, external distillation improved problem-solving, but three forms of self-training did not — and self-training also corrupted previously solved problems at rates above baseline error.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a direct statistical rebuttal to claims that models can reliably bootstrap their own capability through self-training, at least for the methods tested here.

sourceLinks.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null - arXiv

stories.headline: Show HN: Huzzah replaces AI coding prompts with persistent, declarative pseudocode files
stories.summary: Huzzah has developers write design intent as declarative pseudocode in .hz files instead of longform chat prompts; saving the file generates the real code, and editing the pseudocode captures a diff that regenerates only the affected sections. The author argues this fixes three problems with prompt-driven coding agents: prompts that are imperative, transient, and carry unnecessary natural-language overhead.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete attempt to make AI-generated code traceable back to a persistent, editable specification rather than a one-off chat transcript.

sourceLinks.title: Huzzah – a novel approach to coding with AI
